claims.statement: The direct readout has an exploratory sign-odd response, dominated by sin(2 theta)
claims.method: Alternative variance model: at each angle the + arms (0,3) share one returned circuit and the - arms (1,2) another, so the within-configuration differences give an empirical per-setting variance with 10 df; t test of each coefficient against that variance. Mode split and correlation with outside-block fraction.
claims.falsifier: The sin(2 theta) coefficient losing significance under the replicate variance, or tracking the outside-block background
claims.evidence: Replicate-variance t(10) for sin(2 theta): -7.56 (p 1.9e-5) job-00, -16.54 (p 1.4e-8) job-01; replicate variance is 0.83x and 0.44x the binomial value, so counting noise is not underestimated. The signal sits in mode 3 (s2 -0.00901/-0.01062), not mode 2 (-0.0006/-0.0002); the sign-odd transform of the outside fraction has opposite s2 signs in the two jobs (-0.0022/+0.0050) and D-ideal vs outside fraction has Spearman 0.10/0.17 (n.s.).
claims.opposition: Sign is perfectly aliased with compiled configuration: the effect is a difference between two returned meshes per angle, and job-01 re-ran the same 64 compiled circuits, so it replicates a configuration effect rather than testing a sign effect. The coefficient was chosen after inspecting both jobs. The compiled-circuit statistics lie within 2.2e-4 of ideal (registry ascella-signed-coherence-device-diagnostics), so the returned matrices do not predict it. A crossed-compilation acquisition is the falsifier.
